subject: Business Models
title: Data Portability
description: A short lesson to help you apply Data Portability.

hook.text: Imagine if you could move your Facebook friends, photos, and posts to a new social network instantly.

buildup.text: Data portability means users can export their data and take it to a competitor with minimal friction.

discovery.text: The EU's GDPR requires data portability. You have the legal right to download your data from any platform.

twist.text: Having your data is useless without the network. Exporting your Facebook data doesn't bring your friends along.

climax.text: True portability requires interoperability—platforms must actually work together. That's much harder.

punchline.text: You can export your data. Your network stays behind.

quiz.question: Why is data portability alone insufficient to enable platform switching?
options: The network and connections don't transfer with data

details.summary: Data portability is the right of users to export their data from one platform and import it into a competing service. Regulations like GDPR mandate portability to reduce switching costs, while platforms invest in export tools that comply with requirements while minimizing competitive damage.
details.whyItMatters: Data portability directly threatens platform lock-in by reducing switching costs. If users can easily take their data, photos, posts, and connections to a competitor, platforms must compete on ongoing value rather than information captivity.
takeaways: Portability rights let users export their data to competing platforms
GDPR and DMA mandate data portability for European users
Platforms comply minimally, making export possible but not seamless

faq.question: How effective is data portability at reducing platform lock-in?
faq.answer: Limited in practice. While users can export their own data, they cannot export their network connections or the social graph. Moving your photos to a new platform is useless if your friends stay behind. True portability requires network-level interoperability.

faq.question: What data do platforms typically allow users to export?
faq.answer: Photos, posts, friend lists, messages, and profile information are commonly exportable. However, algorithmic recommendations, social graph positions, reputation scores, and years of behavioral data that trained personalization are generally not portable between platforms.
